The Defence Headquarters has denied any ceasefire agreement with Boko Haram, the Islamic State West Africa Province and other criminal groups. The military high command noted that operations against terrorists and kidnappers will continue across the country. The denial comes amid a report that the Federal Government had entered into a secret ceasefire agreement with the Boko Haram faction led by Bakura Doro, which reportedly contributed to relative calm in parts of the North-East for about three months. The report, citing three people with contacts among senior Boko Haram members, said the truce had been in effect since June and was expected to be extended. However, speaking at the joint security briefing in Abuja, the Director of Defence Information, Maj. Gen. Samaila Uba said the military was sustaining pressure on the armed groups, citing the number of terrorists neutralised, suspects arrested and kidnapped victims rescued during recent operations as evidence that troops were not relenting. “On the issue of whether there is a ceasefire with Boko Haram, I want to make it clear that there is nothing like a ceasefire. “Considering the terrorists neutralised, suspects arrested, victims rescued and other successes recorded across our operations, it is clear that we are not relenting. “We will continue to sustain pressure on these criminal elements,” he added. They also target kidnappers and other criminal elements who take up arms against innocent citizens,” Uba said. He warned that individuals involved in criminal activities would either be neutralised through lawful military operations or brought to justice. “Anyone involved in criminal activities that threaten the lives and security of Nigerians will either be eliminated through lawful military operations or brought to justice,” he said. On reports of insurgents moving into parts of the country where they were previously less active, Uba described the development as evidence of the impact of ongoing military operations but said the Armed Forces were not taking the situation lightly. However, I assure you that we are not taking the situation lightly,” he said. Uba cited the recent neutralisation of a high-level terrorist in a forest area as evidence that insurgents would not find safe havens anywhere in the country. “What we are doing is mapping out all the locations where we believe they may have relocated and taking proactive measures to prevent them from establishing footholds in those areas,” he added. The DDI also disclosed that recent adjustments to the Armed Forces’ order of battle, including the establishment of new formations, battalions and units, were aimed at closing security gaps and strengthening military presence in vulnerable areas. He said the military would sustain its operations to prevent terrorists from expanding their activities to other parts of the country. Releasing the military’s achievement said troops executed 588 distinct security operations in September and October. He said troops neutralised 435 terrorists and bandits, including high-profile commanders such as Ali Mandara, Abba Gajiri, Habu Ikkima, Nakif Yana Faruk, Commander Gogore and Abdussamad Ohida. Uba said troops arrested 809 suspects, secured the voluntary surrender of 198 insurgents and successfully liberated 717 kidnapped victims and captives. He listed rescued victims to include 20 prospective NYSC members in Owerri, Imo State and 11 individuals in Danko-Wasagu, Kebbi State. According to him, troops recorded major tactical breakthroughs in Buniyadi, Baga, Kukawa, Bittai and the Owo forest, which severely fractured enemy networks. Uba said that to dismantle their war-making capacity, troops recovered 5,666 arms, ammunition, explosives and Improvised Explosive Devices, alongside vital logistical assets.
